subsystems.name: Agent platform
subsystems.role: the individual robot — small, cheap and expendable enough that losing some does not stop the mission.

subsystems.name: Local sensing and ranging
subsystems.role: lets each agent know a little about its neighbours and surroundings without a global map.

subsystems.name: Mesh communication
subsystems.role: passes messages agent-to-agent so information spreads across the swarm as a relay network.

subsystems.name: Coordination layer
subsystems.role: runs the simple local rules whose interactions produce useful group behaviour.

subsystems.name: Human–swarm interface
subsystems.role: lets operators set intent and constraints rather than steering each robot.

subsystems.name: Logistics and recovery
subsystems.role: gets the swarm to the site, charges it and takes it home.

buildSteps.title: Choose the agent
buildSteps.detail: Pick a body — ground rover, quadcopter or micro-drone — balancing cost, endurance and payload, because cheap agents are what make large numbers possible.

buildSteps.title: Decide what each agent can sense
buildSteps.detail: Only a handful of onboard sensors and short-range neighbour detection are assumed; anything global must be inferred by the group.

buildSteps.title: Design the local rules
buildSteps.detail: Write rules that use only local information — move away from close neighbours, move toward the average heading, mark a spot as visited — and simulate them.

buildSteps.title: Build the communication layer
buildSteps.detail: Implement a mesh radio protocol with gossip-style message passing, tolerant of agents dropping in and out.

buildSteps.title: Test in simulation at scale
buildSteps.detail: Run tens of thousands of simulated agents to check that the rules scale, do not oscillate and degrade gracefully as agents fail.

buildSteps.title: Trial with real hardware
buildSteps.detail: Fly or drive tens to low hundreds of units in a controlled area, comparing real behaviour with the simulation.

buildSteps.title: Add the human layer
buildSteps.detail: Give operators a way to state goals and forbidden zones, plus a single command that recalls every agent.

buildSteps.title: Deploy on a real task
buildSteps.detail: Run supervised missions such as mapping a disaster site or sampling a plume, then analyse where global behaviour diverged from intent.

prerequisites.why: swarm behaviour only pays off when agents cost little enough that many can be fielded.
the swarm needs a network that still works when nodes move, fail or leave range.
flocking, coverage and task allocation are well studied in simulation but less proven with hundreds of real, noisy robots.
indoors, underground, underwater and under jamming, agents must agree on where they are using only each other and local sensing.
small agents fly or drive for tens of minutes, which caps how long a swarm can act independently.

pathway.milestone: supervised swarms for inspection, mapping and drone shows
pathway.unlocks: practical experience operating many vehicles at once.

pathway.milestone: fully decentralised field trials, such as DARPA's OFFSET programme
pathway.unlocks: confidence that emergent control works under real radio and terrain conditions.

pathway.milestone: heterogeneous teams of air and ground robots sharing tasks
pathway.unlocks: disaster response and environmental sensing at a coverage no single robot can reach.

pathway.milestone: large, self-organising meshes with minimal human input on long missions
pathway.unlocks: cheap, resilient monitoring of forests, oceans and infrastructure — provided localisation, energy and safety are solved.
